the spectroscopy of nuclei close to the drip lines and in particular of the weakly bound nucleus (9)(26F).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proton-neutrons effective force is not well understood in the sd shell and that the three-body force is not negligible in the weak binding regime.

the proton-neuron effective interaction is not as strong as it has been thought in the past, and that three-body forces and continuum effects play an important role in the description of weakly bound nuclei.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proton-neutrons interaction in the 0d(5)0f(7) shell is dominated by two-body forces, but the three-body forces and continuum coupling effects are important for the proper description of the low- lying states in (26)(9)F.

the proton-neuron interaction in the (0p1/2)(0p3/2)(0f5/2) shell has to be reduced to account for the weakly bound nature of (9)(25,26)F nuclei, and that three-body interactions are needed to describe the low-lying states of (26)F.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the proton-neuron effective interaction in the sd shell is weaker than expected.
the spectroscopic information of (26)F, which is a weakly bound system, is very important for constraining nuclear effective interactions.
the spectroscopy of weakly bound nuclei is a very powerful probe to study the effective proton-neutron interaction.
